title: GraphGWAS v0.1.5: relational fine-mapping of causal GWAS variants on a multi-omics knowledge graph
description: GraphGWAS is a graph-native fine-mapping platform that carries multi-omics biological structure (genes, tissue-specific eQTLs, pathways, protein-protein interactions) through the inference as a typed factor graph rather than as flat per-variant annotation priors. Matches state-of-the-art Bayesian fine-mappers (SuSiE, FINEMAP, SuSiE-inf, FINEMAP-inf, SBayesRC) at 6-60x the speed under strong signal, and wins 27-2 head-to-head against SuSiE at weak signal with tissue-specific eQTL priors. The v0.1.5 release adds three mixture-prior posterior reweighting methods (GAFM-MX, HBP-MX, ENS) that import a SBayesRC-style 4-component Wakefield Bayes-factor reweighting on the LD-deconvolved z-scores; on the panel-matched 3000 Rice Genomes grain weight + shape pass, GAFM-MX/HBP-MX/ENS each achieve 10/21 (47.6%) top-1-PIP exact-position recovery against the Niu 2021 21-stable-QTN catalogue (highest of any method tested; SuSiE 28.6%, SBayesRC 14.3%). This deposit accompanies the Nature Genetics manuscript 'Relational biological structure improves fine-mapping of causal GWAS variants under weak signal' (Estaji et al., 2026). Contents: pre-built graph-database dumps for 1000 Genomes + multi-omics (17 GB) and yeast 1011 Genomes (0.5 GB); benchmark outputs (JSON + TSV) for every figure and table in the paper, including the 79-replicate weak-signal 27-2 headline run and the v0.1.5 mixture-prior cross-species + 3kRG outputs; Pan-UK Biobank cross-ancestry fine-mapping outputs; the 3kRG IRRI 18-trait whole-genome scan summary statistics and the 4-trait grain weight + shape pass; figure source data; simulation seeds and per-replicate logs; pre-registered control experiments (placebo prior, null-overlap permutation, hyperparameter sensitivity); and a source-code snapshot at the submission tag.
